title: 3.3.0 release: no suite rides the Windows time cap
description: P126 landed with CI green once on windows-latest, then the next round timed out both suites at the 300s cap with no change to their subjects: they ride the limit. This holds the 3.3.0 release.
desiredOutcome: test_commit_task_work and test_drive_phase finish on windows-latest with clear margin under the sweep's per-file cap in repeated CI runs, through staged blocks sized to the runner, with case ids and verdicts unchanged.

findings.file: plugins/audit/tests/_harness.py:688-706 (stage_workers) with tools/sweep-selftests.py default_jobs CI branch
findings.issue: The stage pool was sized for a premise the phase itself contradicts, and it does not consult the sweep pool it now shares cores with. P127.1 sizes for a 'two-core windows-latest runner' (stage_workers docstring; description), but run 38324787932 printed 'sweep: 331 files, 2 workers', which default_jobs() only prints for 4 cpus (cpus-2), and P127.2's own ci.yml comment says the same ('16.7 minutes of suites on two workers'). On a 4-vCPU runner stage_workers(4) == 2, so test_drive_phase's wall time has a floor of (serial stage sum)/2: the task's own numbers are 438-459s serial on macOS, i.e. ~220s on an idle mac pair before any Windows process-start penalty, against the 280s STAGE_TIMEOUT and 300s file cap. Before the phase it had up to 6 children. P127.2 then gives the sweep every core under CI=true (4 workers) and costliest-first submission, so in the shard holding test_drive_phase (shard 2 in the committed table, with test__invariants 118, run_test_gate 60, full_gate 57 started beside it) about 5 processes contend for 4 cores while the heavy staged suite is capped at 2 of them. The same cap now also applies to test_audit_task and test_close_phase (both staged_main users, both in shard 1), which the task did not mention or measure. Worst case the two pools multiply (4 sweep workers x 2 stage workers = 8 runnable on 4 cores); the typical case is the opposite, a heavy suite starved of the cores its siblings have already freed. Nothing handed shows the margin: the only evidence is macOS with 14 cores.
findings.resolution: Read the per-file seconds from CI run 38370435884 (jobs 'selftests (windows-latest, plain 2/3)' and shard 1) before accepting this. If test_drive_phase is above ~150s there, size the pool from the machine the sweep leaves free rather than a fixed half: e.g. have run_one export the sweep's worker count in the child env and let stage_workers use max(2, min(STAGE_WORKERS, cpus - sweep_jobs + 1)), or under CI=true give a staged suite min(STAGE_WORKERS, cpus). Correct the 'two-core runner' wording in the stage_workers docstring, the P127.1 description and sr12's label, and extend sr12 to pin the CI case.

findings.issue: A leg can now be dropped from CI with gate-parity green. Before this diff a leg ran iff its step existed in ci.yml, which sweep_leg_drift compares against verify.sh. Now a step runs only if the matrix contains its leg and its `if:` spells it the same: `leg: [plain, cp1252, spaced]` plus the `include` e2e cells. shard_matrix_drift checks only the `shard: [1, 2, 3]` list. Deleting `cp1252` from the `leg:` list, typing `matrix.leg == 'cp1252 '` or `'cp1251'` in a step, or removing the `include` e2e cells leaves every step present in ci.yml, so the leg comparison passes while that leg (or all launcher steps and the runner's own --selftest) never runs. This is exactly the 'leg silently not run' class the parity gate exists for, and the prove-gates row added (shard: [1,2]) only mutates the shard list.
findings.resolution: fixed in P127.3-bgr (915565f66819): Extend shard_matrix_drift (or a sibling) to read every `matrix.leg == '<x>'` in an `if:` and require each <x> to be produced by the matrix (in `leg:` or an `include` entry, and not excluded for every os), and each produced leg to have a step; add a prove-gates TABLE row mutating `leg: [plain, cp1252, spaced]` to drop one, and an ALLOW row for the over-fire.

findings.issue: sr12 pins the stage_workers() table and that the default is within 2..STAGE_WORKERS, but not that run_stages() uses it. Reverting the one-line wiring (`if workers is None: workers = stage_workers()` back to `workers=STAGE_WORKERS`) leaves sr12 and every sr case green, so the behaviour the task names (the pool respects the machine) is pinned only as a pure function. The executor's redFirst is not-attempted, so no run shows otherwise.
findings.resolution: Add a case that runs run_stages over a fixture of labels with a recording stub (or patches stage_workers to return 1) and asserts the concurrency actually used, so the wiring is the thing that fails.

findings.issue: The comments and CONTRIBUTING.md say a stale cost table 'costs balance, never coverage', but sh7 asserts set(sh_costs) <= set(sh_full), so deleting or renaming any swept file turns the sweep's own selftest red (in the e2e cell and in whichever shard holds that file) until someone re-records .github/sweep-costs.json. Either the guard or the sentence is wrong. The table is also one macOS 12-worker run (platform darwin, workers 12); test_commit_task_work is recorded at 57s although P127.1 brought it to ~15s, so the balance is already stale on its first day.
findings.resolution: fixed in P127.4-bgr (2944d2608064): Pick one: drop the subset requirement from sh7 and keep only 'loads, and times most files', or keep it and say in the comments that a rename must re-record the table. Re-record the table from the CI run after P127.1/P127.2 land.

findings.issue: The header's 'longest selftests: 24m59s' bound reasoning and `timeout-minutes: 60` were sized for one job per OS; every cell now targets 4-7 minutes, so a hung cell holds a runner for an hour and the comment's own rule (a bound under twice the figure is refused, and the figure is re-measured when a job changes) has not been applied to the new shape. Job check names also changed from 'selftests (os)' to 'selftests (os, leg shard)' (17 cells), so any branch-protection required-check entry for the old names (not in the repo, unverifiable here) would never report.
findings.resolution: After run 38370435884, rewrite the 'longest selftests' line to the longest cell and set timeout-minutes to at least twice it; confirm the required-checks list on the remote names the new cells or a single aggregate job.

tasks.title: test_commit_task_work and test_drive_phase run as right-sized staged blocks and finish well under the cap on a two-core runner
tasks.description: CI evidence, two rounds on windows-latest (2 cores): run 38324787932 (ci/p126 @ 0aca587b) both suites passed; run 38333046789 (ci/p126 @ 46462e88, no change to either suite's subject) '--- plugins/audit/tests/test_commit_task_work.py: did not finish within 300s ---' and the same for test_drive_phase.py. So both sit at the sweep's 300s per-file cap on Windows and pass or fail by scheduling noise. Measured on macOS alone (no contention): test_commit_task_work 65s (106 cases, one process), test_drive_phase 103s (237 cases, already STAGES + _harness.staged_main). Windows starts a process several times slower, and both suites are made of git and interpreter starts. Fix by structure, never by raising DEFAULT_TIMEOUT alone: (1) measure each block's wall time (time each `--stage LABEL` run) and record the numbers in the return; (2) give test_commit_task_work a STAGES table and hand its __main__ to staged_main(), as test_drive_phase does, keeping its case ids and order as the replay contract requires; (3) rebalance test_drive_phase so no single stage holds most of its time (split the heaviest block along its existing case functions); (4) make the stage pool size respect the machine: _harness.STAGE_WORKERS is a fixed 6 while a windows-latest runner has 2 cores and the sweep already runs suites on them - use min(STAGE_WORKERS, a share of os.cpu_count()) and say why; (5) reduce per-case process starts where a fixture repo can be built once per block instead of once per case. Target: each suite's slowest stage well under STAGE_TIMEOUT and the whole suite under half the sweep cap on macOS, measured twice with a gap. The orchestrator verifies on windows-latest CI.

outcome.technical: test_commit_task_work.py: the single _cases body (inline ordinary run plus chained verdict/scope/branch/empty-gate/retired-red/gate-identity/kept-deletion calls and six nested stage() blocks) is now 17 STAGES rows handed to _harness.staged_main (prefix ctw-stages-); inline part cut at its existing section comments into _ordinary_cases/_declared_cases/_records_cases; every block takes (check) via a new @_own_repos decorator that builds and closes its own Repos; chain calls removed, old nested stage labels (cl/sl/dp/ae/bl/ce) reused as row labels. 106 case ids, labels and order identical to HEAD (diff of PASS/FAIL line prefixes of the HEAD file run vs new run: identical). test_drive_phase.py: two cuts along existing section comments, _drive_cases -> + _drive_mutant_cases (row dpm-block), _signoff_cases -> + _signoff_findings_cases (row sgf-block), placed right after their parents so replay order is unchanged; 237/237. _harness.py: new stage_workers(cpus=None) = max(2, min(STAGE_WORKERS, cpus//2)); run_stages(workers=None) uses it (a 2-core runner no longer gets 6 children sharing 2 cores while the sweep runs beside it; floor 2 because blocks wait on children); selftest case sr12 pins the table. DEFAULT_TIMEOUT untouched. MEASUREMENTS (macOS 14 cores, load avg ~10 largely from my own runs, each twice with 20s gap; per-stage = each stage run alone, serially). test_commit_task_work BEFORE (one process): full wall 58.9s / 60.4s; per-function: index 5.1, verdict+scope+branch+empty-gate chain 26.4 (scope 5.9, branch 7.0, empty-gate chain 8.4), inline ordinary run ~22 (derived), attempt 4.5; no stages existed so slowest unit = whole file. AFTER: full wall 15.4s / 14.7s; serial stage sum 57.5s / 69.1s over 17 stages; slowest br-block 9.1s / 9.9s (sc 5.9/8.5, vd 7.0/8.4). test_drive_phase BEFORE: full wall 84.0s (one run); serial stage sum 372.6s / 409.5s over 51 stages; slowest sg-block 26.6s / 29.5s, then dp-block 20.8/19.6, w1 15.7/16.0, dk 14.5/18.4. AFTER: full wall 88.6s / 86.4s (unchanged within load noise: CPU-bound, 6 workers on this box either way); serial sum 438.1s / 459.1s over 53 stages; slowest dk-block 19.2s / 22.1s, sgf 14.8/19.6, sg 14.3 (was 26.6-29.5), dpm 14.0. Stage cap 280s: both far under; whole-suite wall under half of the 300s cap on macOS (ctw ~15s, dp ~87s). NOT DONE / HONEST LIMIT: item 5 (build a fixture repo once per block) not changed. Profiling sg-block showed nearly all its time is Python CLI script launches (audit-task.py 28 launches 8.3s, drive-phase.py 15 launches 5.9s, run-test-gate 14 launches 3.5s) which the cases exist to exercise; _repo() already costs only 3 git starts and ctw's per-case repos are by design (cases mutate git). So test_drive_phase's total CPU (~370-460s serial) is not reduced by this task; on 2 cores it relies on stage_workers() sizing and finer blocks, and the orchestrator's windows-latest run is the real evidence. test_commit_task_work went from one serial process to parallel blocks (about 4x wall on macOS). Gates: sweep-selftests summary line '331/331 files ok, 15799 cases' seen (exit read through a tail pipe); ruff all checks passed; vermin exit 0; _harness.py --selftest all pass.
outcome.descriptive: test_commit_task_work now runs as 17 parallel staged blocks (60s -> 15s wall on macOS), test_drive_phase's two heaviest blocks are split (slowest stage ~28s -> ~20s), and the stage pool is half the cores (min 2, max 6) instead of a fixed 6; case ids and order unchanged.

tasks.title: CI runs each sweep leg as its own parallel job, sharded, on every core - one plugin's CI finishes in about ten minutes
tasks.description: Owner, 2026-10-13: CI for one repo and one plugin must not take enterprise-scale time - change it now. Measured on run 38324787932 (green): windows selftests 34 min = full sweep 16.7 min, then the SAME full sweep again under cp1252 16.4 min; ubuntu selftests 23 min = sweep 7.5 + cp1252 7.7 + spaced 7.2 min, one after another in one job; the sweep prints 'sweep: 331 files, 2 workers' on windows-latest because it keeps all cores but two free, which is right on a workstation and wastes half a CI runner. Restructure without weakening any check: (1) every sweep leg (plain, cp1252, spaced) becomes its own job, running in parallel instead of in sequence; (2) tools/sweep-selftests.py gains `--shard I/N` (a stable, deterministic split of the file list, balanced by recorded or estimated per-file cost so the slow suites do not land together; the union of shards is exactly the full set, pinned by a selftest case) and ci.yml runs each leg as a matrix of shards; (3) the sweep uses every core when it runs in CI (an explicit `--jobs` from ci.yml, or the CI environment), keeping the workstation default; (4) the cheap end-to-end launcher steps stay where they are or move to the shortest job. Keep `!cancelled()` on every independent step and gate-parity green - every leg CI runs must still be named in verify.sh, CONTRIBUTING.md and CLAUDE.md's gate list, so update the descriptions that state how CI runs the sweep (CLAUDE.md says the runner uses 'all cores but two'). Target: CI wall time at or under about 10 minutes, measured on the next CI run and stated in the return as before/after per job.

Measured by the orchestrator on CI run 38370435884 (ci/p127 @ 622d7254, the new sharded matrix): whole run 10m44s (was ~34 min); every ubuntu cell green, 3m-4m; windows cells 4m40s-6m43s, but three red ONLY on the 300s per-file cap: plain 1 (133 files, 4 workers) test__deps.py and test_audit_task.py; plain 2 (99 files, 4 workers) and cp1252 2 test_drive_phase.py. This is R1 as predicted: sweep workers (now all 4 cores in CI) x stage workers (stage_workers(4)=2) oversubscribe the runner while a staged heavy suite needs most of it - test_drive_phase's serial stage sum is ~440s on macOS and Windows starts processes several times slower; before P127 it finished just under 300s with 6 stage children on a 4-core runner. Direction: make the two pools one budget. The heaviest files by the recorded cost table (staged suites first) run in their own matrix cells (a 'heavy' shard per leg, or cost-balanced shards with a per-shard concurrency budget) where the sweep runs them one or two at a time and their stage pool gets the remaining cores (stage workers = cores // concurrent heavy files in CI; keep the workstation rule otherwise); everything else shards as now with workers = cores. A per-file timeout may be derived from the recorded cost (e.g. a multiple of the slowest recorded platform cost, never below 300s) as the hang detector - that is a calibrated limit, not the cap raised alone. Target: every windows cell green with clear margin and the whole run still about 10-11 minutes; state the arithmetic per cell.

tasks.description:
The header's 'longest selftests: 24m59s' bound reasoning and `timeout-minutes: 60` were sized for one job per OS; every cell now targets 4-7 minutes, so a hung cell holds a runner for an hour and the comment's own rule (a bound under twice the figure is refused, and the figure is re-measured when a job changes) has not been applied to the new shape. Job check names also changed from 'selftests (os)' to 'selftests (os, leg shard)' (17 cells), so any branch-protection required-check entry for the old names (not in the repo, unverifiable here) would never report.

Resolution asked: After run 38370435884, rewrite the 'longest selftests' line to the longest cell and set timeout-minutes to at least twice it; confirm the required-checks list on the remote names the new cells or a single aggregate job.
